Character information -> Rooms native text and display branches

Sources are the configured local Steam and official classic PE images. This
file describes static image code. It does not record a game display observation.
The extraction script is tools/extract_character_rooms_sources.py.

Scope
  Steam PE:6a70a6d9:02711000: Rooms switch arm RVA 0x1703f6..0x171554.
  Classic PE:6a70b91c:0270a000: Rooms switch arm RVA 0x170386..0x1714e4.
  Steam room-grade leaf function: 0xab4f20..0xab52d0.
  Classic room-grade leaf function: 0xab1fa0..0xab2350.
  These grade functions have no .pdata unwind entry. They are bounded by
  their actual native leaf entry and the next function entry, not the preceding
  unrelated unwind function.

Grade source decompilation
  Arguments: rcx=output std::string*, edx=value, r8w=room_type.
  The output is cleared first. Unknown room types return an empty string.
  Native dispatch visits types 3, 2, 1, 0. Each type has nine branches.
  The threshold tests, in native descending order, are:
    value >= 10000; value >= 2500; value >= 1500; value >= 1000;
    value >= 500; value >= 250; value >= 100; value > 0; default (value <= 0).
  Every branch tail-calls the shared string assign helper with the complete
  literal and its exact length. Source fields are never assembled from words.

  The following arrays list branches in ascending value order:
  thresholds = {value<=0, 1, 100, 250, 500, 1000, 1500, 2500, 10000}
  room_type 0 (office):
    {"No Study", "Meager Study", "Modest Study", "Study", "Decent Study",
     "Splendid Study", "Throne Room", "Opulent Throne Room", "Royal Throne Room"}
  room_type 1 (bedroom):
    {"No Quarters", "Meager Quarters", "Modest Quarters", "Quarters",
     "Decent Quarters", "Fine Quarters", "Great Bedroom", "Grand Bedroom",
     "Royal Bedroom"}
  room_type 2 (dining room):
    {"No Dining Room", "Meager Dining Room", "Modest Dining Room", "Dining Room",
     "Decent Dining Room", "Fine Dining Room", "Great Dining Room",
     "Grand Dining Room", "Royal Dining Room"}
  room_type 3 (tomb):
    {"No Tomb", "Grave", "Servant's Burial Chamber", "Burial Chamber", "Tomb",
     "Fine Tomb", "Mausoleum", "Grand Mausoleum", "Royal Mausoleum"}

  The 36 complete grade branches and 32 positive requirement branches for
  each edition, with native literal/instruction coordinates, are saved in
  decompiled-text-branches.tsv. The requirement outputs are the literal
  "Needs " plus the complete grade returned for required_value. There is no
  branch named "Needs No Study", "Needs No Quarters", "Needs No Dining Room",
  or "Needs No Tomb": required_value must be positive before drawing it.

Rooms renderer decompilation (Steam coordinates below)
  unit/context = [rsp+0xb260]
  zone_id list = unit+0x1c00
  current room values = unit+0x1c18
  required values[4] = unit+0x114 + room_type*4
  row index = [rsp+0x38c]
  room_type = [rsp+0x390]
  satisfaction = [rsp+0x1f0]

  Setup 0x1703f6..0x17053d:
    visible_count = (panel_bottom - panel_top + 1) / 3;
    total_count = zone_id_list.size();
    If total_count == 0, draw "No assigned rooms" and leave this switch arm.
    If total_count > visible_count, reserve two columns for the scrollbar.
  Scroll and row loop 0x17053d..0x1707b9:
    Clamp the scroll offset into [0, max(0, total_count-visible_count)].
    Visit rows until either visible_count or total_count is reached.
    Each list entry occupies three native grid rows. Draw its background.
  Zone/type branch 0x1707b9..0x1709aa:
    zone = building_id_lookup(zone_id_list[row]);
    native_type = room_type = -1;
    If zone exists, native_type = zone->virtual_type() via vtable+0xd8.
    Otherwise map synthetic zone IDs:
      -1 -> native_type 0x5d; -2 -> 0x5c; -3 -> 0x50; -4 -> 0x61.
    Then map native_type:
      0x5d -> room_type 0; 0x5c -> room_type 1;
      0x50 -> room_type 2; 0x61 -> room_type 3; otherwise -> -1.
  Satisfaction and icon branch 0x1709aa..0x1710c0:
    satisfaction = -1;
    If room_type != -1 and required_values[room_type] > 0:
      If required_values[room_type] <= current_values[row], satisfaction = 0.
      Else if current_values[row] > 0, satisfaction = 1.
      Else satisfaction = 2.
    Draw a 4-by-3 icon from the native atlas:
      room_type 0: no requirement 0x136, missing 0x137,
                   insufficient 0x138, satisfied 0x139;
      room_type 1: no requirement 0x132, missing 0x133,
                   insufficient 0x134, satisfied 0x135;
      room_type 2: no requirement 0x13a, missing 0x13b,
                   insufficient 0x13c, satisfied 0x13d;
      room_type 3: no requirement 0x13e, missing 0x13f,
                   insufficient 0x140, satisfied 0x141.
    Unknown native types have no room icon. A native graphics flag selects
    whether the icon cells invoke the additional native tile rendering call.
  Room name branch 0x1710c0..0x171165:
    Draw the building name only if zone exists and its string at zone+0xd0
    is nonempty. Set white (color 7). Draw at the room row's text column.
    Exact name construction/getName branches are owned by names sources
    beside this file; this renderer reads the supplied complete name.
  Actual room grade 0x171165..0x17120e:
    Set white (color 7). Set the cursor to text column, row_y+1.
    actual = room_grade(current_values[row], room_type);
    Draw the complete actual string even when zone is missing. That is why
    synthetic missing-room rows retain their correct "No ..." grade.
  Requirement branch 0x17120e..0x17136f:
    If room_type == -1 or required_values[room_type] <= 0, skip this line.
    Select color: satisfaction 2 -> 4 (red), 1 -> 6 (yellow), else -> 2 (green).
    Set cursor to text column, row_y+2.
    required = room_grade(required_values[room_type], room_type);
    addst("Needs ", r8b=3, r9d=0);
    addst(required, r8d=0, r9d=0);
    These are two native draws belonging to one complete requirement field.
    The color was set separately. Native addst at Steam RVA 0xad9960..0xad9a33
    does not read its incoming r8 justification argument. It copies the string,
    optionally applies the r9 width, then calls addchar(0xbb190, byte, true)
    for each byte at the current cursor. Thus r8b=3 here does not select a
    different font or baseline: prefix and suffix advance one continuous row.
  Action and scrollbar 0x17136f..0x171554:
    If zone exists, draw its 3-by-3 action icon in the existing right gutter.
    If zone is absent, skip the action. Advance row_y by three and loop.
    After rows, render the scrollbar only when total_count > visible_count,
    retaining the stored scroll offset and native scroll UI flag.

Native text draw return coordinates (RVA)
  field                 Steam return    Classic return    native r8 / r9
  No assigned rooms     0x170529        0x1704b9          0 / 0
  zone/name             0x171164        0x1710f4          0 / 0
  actual room grade     0x17120d        0x17119d          0 / 0
  Needs prefix          0x171337        0x1712c7          3 / 0
  requirement grade     0x171360        0x1712f0          0 / 0

All five source fields use the same native text column (left+8). The grade
and requirement cursor rows are row_y+1 and row_y+2, respectively. The name
may be absent. These source locations and the complete native logical row
are the semantic owners; generic standalone words cannot infer their role.
